rows.observed strokes: A short left arm curves into a rounded right-hand loop with a visible enclosed light centre. The stem descends well below the loop. This differs from the same-page psi exemplar, whose separate central upright and right arm leave an open upper bowl.

The left arm curls into a small right-hand oval/loop and the joined stem descends with a slight rightward foot. The right-hand loop is compact and dark but its return into the central junction is visible; there is no separate tall middle prong of the page's psi form.

The leading rounded bowl joins a tall oblique ascender; a second tall narrow loop follows, then a later upright and a low terminal curl. The strokes are closely joined, so the initial bowl plus ascender can be divided as d or as al. No clear detached accents or deep j descender are visible in this crop, unlike the later deja exemplar on this page. The division de là is visually plausible, but these features do not establish the whole word confidently.

The short left hook connects to a clearly closed, elongated right oval; from the loop junction a stem descends and turns slightly right. The enclosed loop distinguishes this from the open, separately pronged psi elsewhere on this same page.

After the opening parenthesis a low rise and a short upright survive above the cancellation bar, but the bar merges their baseline and prevents a secure et reading. Farther right, immediately before phi, a taller curved l-shaped stem and short rightward e-like tick remain distinct enough to read le.

In the upper crossed-out line the group following phi has several uprights and kinks whose baseline joins are hidden by the bar. The final tall looped stem followed by a low terminal arch supports la. The lower crossed-out continuation has a tall initial fork and adjacent loop, isolated above-line marks, two visible below-line strokes, and a closing parenthesis; the cancellation conceals too many joins to certify the full word réciproque or the preceding est.

The isolated cancelled interlinear group preserves a small hooked crossing stroke at the left, then a small oval and short taller loop/ascender farther right. A continuous horizontal cancellation stroke occupies the baseline across the entire group. These remnants do not securely distinguish the proposed e and t.
